subject: Request: temporary latency margin for canary model launch
messages:
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Maria Sanchez <maria.sanchez@pulsemetrics.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Request: temporary latency margin for canary model launch

Hi Maria —

Thanks again for the quick sync this morning. As we discussed, Pulsemetrics intends to flip on canary traffic to the new gen2-compact model next week for 10% of live requests. The model shows strong quality gains but we observed a 20–30ms median latency uplift in the canary runs compared to our current baseline.

Before you ramp more traffic we want to put a temporary agreement in place to avoid surprising SLO alerts on your side and ours. Proposed asks:
- Accept a temporary, bounded latency margin of +35ms p50 for the canary cohort for up to 72 hours after the initial cutover.
- Redwood will enable conservative batching and a KB cache warm-up; we will also monitor and revert routing automatically if p95 exceeds +150ms.
- We'll share a short canary traffic report and a rollback playbook (attached).

If Pulsemetrics agrees, we can capture this as a one-time addendum to the existing SLA and proceed with the canary on Monday 9/21. If you prefer, legal can sign a short amendment.

Attached: canary_traffic_report.csv (sample), proposed_slo_patch_v1.pdf, jra-1458-canary-plan.md

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0129
---
Redwood Inference | developer-first inference runtime
From: Maria Sanchez <maria.sanchez@pulsemetrics.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 15:05:34 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary latency margin for canary model launch

Dev —

Appreciate the detail. Quick clarifying Qs: is the +35ms p50 an expected steady-state for the next 72 hours or a one-time cold-start spike? We need to understand our customer-facing dashboards — if our p50 jumps visibly we get churn questions.

Also, can you confirm the rollback trigger and who owns the cutover window? We prefer a joint abort threshold.

If you can outline the exact monitoring checks and the person on-call, I can fast-track approval from Ops.

—Maria
Head of Platform, Pulsemetrics
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:11 -0700
Subject: internal: Pulsemetrics canary SLA margin request (prep for legal/ops)

Folks —

Looping in legal/ops context before we confirm with Maria. Summary: Pulsemetrics asks to accept +35ms p50 for canary cohort for 72 hours. They want joint rollback triggers.

Notes for review:
- Risk: brief latency uplift increases customer-facing p50; but it’s bounded and we can auto-fallback.
- Mitigations: throttled rollout (10%), automatic route fallback, real-time alerting to Pulsemetrics and Redwood SREs.
- Ask of Legal/Contracts: one-paragraph one-time amendment capturing the window, metrics, and rollback authority. No billing change.

I've attached the proposed_slo_patch_v1.pdf with exact metric language. Can we get Ops sign-off on the p95 abort threshold and the on-call contact? Lauren — can you coordinate SRE? Marissa — you’re on deck for the contract blurb.

Thanks,
Rishi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 11:03:45 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: Pulsemetrics canary SLA margin request (prep for legal/ops)

Rishi / team —

Ops accepts the temporary window with conditions:
- Abort/fallback if p95 latency for the canary cohort exceeds +150ms relative to baseline for more than 5 minutes.
- Immediate escalation to on-call SRE: Priya Natarajan (priya_natarajan@redwood.com).
- Redwood will enable conservative batching and prefix cache warm-up; we will not apply aggressive quantization during the canary.
- We ask Pulsemetrics to limit canary traffic to 10% and hold business-hours cutover (09:00–17:00 PT) for the first day.

If those are acceptable, Legal can issue a short amendment. I’ll loop Priya on the runbook.

—Lauren
Director, Platform Operations
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Maria Sanchez <maria.sanchez@pulsemetrics.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Sep 2026 08:22:10 -0700
Subject: Re: Request: temporary latency margin for canary model launch

Maria —

Legal here. We can accept the temporary latency margin by adding a short one-paragraph amendment to the existing MSA. Key points in the amendment:
- Scope: one canary cohort (<=10% traffic) for up to 72 hours starting at agreed cutover.
- Metrics: p50 uplift allowance +35ms; abort if p95 > +150ms for >5 minutes.
- No billing or SLO credit impacts for this window; both parties reserve the right to pause.

If Pulsemetrics confirms the monitoring contact (Priya will be on-call for Redwood) and the preferred cutover window (we recommend Mon 2026-09-21 09:00 PT), Legal will produce the amendment and a DocuSign link.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Maria Sanchez <maria.sanchez@pulsemetrics.ai>

Subject: Re: Request: temporary latency margin for canary model launch

Maria —

Thanks — sounds like we’re aligned. Quick recap and next steps:
1) Pulsemetrics confirms the cutover window: Monday, 2026-09-21, 09:00 PT (business hours) — please reply to confirm.
2) Redwood will open the DocuSign amendment (one paragraph) capturing the metric allowances and rollback triggers.
3) Priya Natarajan (priya_natarajan@redwood.com) will be on-call for the canary with the listed abort threshold.
4) We’ll share a live canary dashboard and the initial canary_traffic_report.csv within the first hour of cutover.

If you confirm the date we’ll send the DocuSign link and finalize the runbook.

Appreciate the fast coordination,
Dev
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
